answer: An agent network can issue each identity a short-lived credential only after it completes a randomly assigned task whose result is checked against several independently chosen peers, with rewards weighted by a history of accurate reviews. Creating thousands of identities then does not multiply influence: each must spend compute and time on tasks, and new accounts lack trusted review history. Like a tide shaping a river around a knoll, diverse reviewers make it harder to steer consensus with a cheap swarm.
